title: Grit
description: Passion and perseverance for long‑term goals. It’s not talent; it’s sustained effort over years, even after failure.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Passion and perseverance for long‑term goals. It’s not talent; it’s sustained effort over years, even after failure.

sections.title: Core Characteristics
content: Consistency of interest: not jumping from passion to passion.
Perseverance of effort: working through setbacks, maintaining effort despite plateaus.

sections.title: Behavioral Patterns
content: Gritty individuals practice the same skill for years, show up even when unmotivated, and treat setbacks as part of the process.
Low‑grit individuals switch goals frequently, abandon pursuits when they become difficult, or lose interest once the novelty fades.

sections.title: Communication Style
content: Gritty: “I’m not there yet,” “I’ll figure it out,” focuses on long‑term progress.
Low grit: “I’m bored of this,” “It’s not working,” “Maybe I’m not meant for this.”

sections.title: Strengths
content: Predicts achievement in challenging domains (military, education, competitive fields) better than IQ.

sections.title: Weaknesses
content: Can become stubborn pursuit of a dead‑end goal.
Ignoring feedback that suggests a pivot.

sections.title: Decision-Making Style
content: Sticks with chosen path; may refuse to cut losses when needed.

sections.title: Relationship Patterns
sections.content: Gritty people apply the same persistence to relationships: they work through rough patches.

sections.title: Workplace Behavior
sections.content: Reliable, long‑term contributors. They finish what they start.

sections.title: Leadership Style
sections.content: Lead by example, persistent, but may push teams too hard toward a rigid vision.

sections.title: Stress Response
sections.content: Sees stress as a challenge to overcome, not a threat to avoid.

sections.title: How to Identify It
sections.content: Ask: “What’s the longest you’ve ever worked on a single project, and how did you handle the boring parts?”

sections.title: Common Misconceptions
content: Grit is not about grinding 24/7; it’s consistent effort, not burnout.
It can be developed; it’s not fixed.

sections.title: Real-World Scenario
sections.content: Two cadets enter West Point. One is naturally athletic; the other struggles but never quits. The natural drops out after the first brutal summer; the gritty cadet graduates. Grit, not talent, predicted survival.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Talent is the starting gun; grit is the legs that carry you to the finish line. The gun doesn’t run the race.
